HasUponPickupEffect.rationale: Matches EmptyCage.cs:14; drives RelicModel.IsTradable (RelicModel.cs:176-190) mirrored at relics/base.py:126-136. Rule 7: those two files are unhashed here.

AfterObtained.issue: Rollup of guard N2 per binding rule 4. The count (CardsVar(2), EmptyCage.cs:16, vs CARDS = 2, empty_cage.py:16), the candidate filter (N1) and the removal itself all match -- executed: a fresh run's 10-card deck goes to 8. The only divergence is that the sim substitutes a seeded random pick for the game's player-choice screen, which also consumes RNG the game does not.

guards.rationale: CardModel.IsRemovable is exactly `!Keywords.Contains(CardKeyword.Eternal)` (CardModel.cs:737) and run.removable_cards() is exactly `[c for c in self.deck if not c.eternal]`. FromDeckForRemoval passes no additional filter here (EmptyCage.cs:20 supplies only prefs and player), so the two candidate sets are the same set. Its sortingOrder lambda -- curses first via -999999999 (CardSelectCmd.cs:624) -- is the select screen's display order and has no effect on which cards are removable. Executed (py audit/tools/relic_probes_b05.py cage-feather): a starting deck contains no Eternal cards, so both sides offer all 10. Rule 7: CardSelectCmd.cs, CardModel.cs and run.py are unhashed here.

guards.what: N2: run.select_cards falls back to `self.rng.sample` when no card_selector is installed (run.py:371-390), where the game opens a removal screen and draws no RNG
guards.issue: Same mechanism and same verdict as relic/electric_shrymp guard N3 in this batch (binding rule 3): C#'s FromDeckGeneric (CardSelectCmd.cs:636-677) reaches either the Selector, the local UI screen or a remote choice, none of which consumes an Rng, while the sim's default picks with the run's shared legacy random.Random -- so the sim removes different cards AND advances a stream the game does not. DORMANT for RL play and for the conformance harness (the runner installs run.card_selector from the replay's SelectGridCard commands, so the fallback is not taken); live for any parity run that reaches the Darv shrine's Empty Cage with no selector installed. Rule 7: CardSelectCmd.cs and run.py are unhashed here.

guards.what: N3: C# removes one card at a time through `await CardPileCmd.RemoveFromDeck(item)` inside a foreach (EmptyCage.cs:20-23); the sim removes the whole selection in one run.remove_cards call (empty_cage.py:19-20)
guards.rationale: Both iterate the SAME selection list, which is computed in full before the first removal on either side, so no removal can change the candidate set mid-loop. run.remove_cards (run.py:356-358) is itself a per-card loop over deck.remove. The one thing the sim's path lacks is any deck-removal hook -- but the game has none either: CardPileCmd.RemoveFromDeck fires no Hook that AbstractModel declares for relics, so there is no listener to skip. Rule 7: run.py is unhashed here.

guards.what: N4: `!prefs.RequireManualConfirmation && list.Count <= prefs.MinSelect` auto-keeps the whole list (CardSelectCmd.cs:653-655) when the deck holds 2 or fewer removable cards
guards.rationale: run.select_cards clamps to `min(count, len(candidates))` and returns [] for an empty list (run.py:384-386), so a 1-card or 2-card removable deck removes 1 or 2 on both sides. Recorded because the C# edge is guarded by a prefs flag whose value this record cannot see (CardSelectorPrefs is not read here) -- but the outcome is the same either way: with RequireManualConfirmation set, C# opens a screen whose only possible answers are the same 1 or 2 cards.

guards.what: N5: CanonicalVars / ExtraHoverTips (EmptyCage.cs:16) and the removal-screen prompt string
guards.rationale: RelicModel.Flash() / base.Status = RelicStatus.* / ShowCounter / DisplayAmount / InvokeDisplayAmountChanged / CanonicalVars / ExtraHoverTips / Cmd.Wait / VfxCmd / CardCmd.Preview are presentation only -- the relic bar's glow, counter and hover text, the damage/heal numbers and animation timing. The sim has no relic UI. Waived under the shared contract's presentation/animation exclusion, not under an unreachability claim.
